about.title: About
about.description: How the photos happen: walks, available light, and bad weather.
about.quote: One camera and a walk until something looks right.
about.intro: deney is a photographer drawn to available light and late hours: snow-lit streets, buildings with warm windows, sunsets through branches, and quiet harbors. No heavy setups, no studio tricks. One camera and a walk until something looks right.

sections.heading: Style
sections.body: Mostly dark scenes with a single strong light source, weather in the frame, and compositions that let the scene breathe. The work is moody rather than polished, and the mood comes from what the light is doing, not from editing.

sections.heading: What deney shoots
sections.body: Night streets in winter, fog and snow, empty courtyards, old buildings with lit windows, sunsets over hills, and harbors at first light. If the weather is bad, that is usually the best time to go out.
